input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: The shape check before Editor.edit_files tests only for os.PathLike and no longer wraps a plain str, so a string filename is passed on as an iterable and consumed character by character when building the editor command.
- failure path: click.edit(filename="notes.txt") launches the editor with the nine single-character files n, o, t, e, s, ., t, x, t instead of notes.txt; saving creates stray files in the working directory and the intended file is never opened.

Reviewer finding
- description: String filenames are no longer wrapped as a single path, so existing calls such as `click.edit(filename="notes.txt")` pass individual characters as filenames to the editor.
- rationale: When `filename` is a string, the new `isinstance(filename, os.PathLike)` check is false. The string reaches `edit_files` as an iterable of characters, causing the editor to open files named after those characters instead of the requested file. Include `str` alongside `os.PathLike` in the check.
critique: The finding points to the same cause as the label: the isinstance check covers only os.PathLike, so a str filename reaches edit_files and is iterated character by character. It also gives the same failure, with click.edit(filename="notes.txt") opening single-character files.
